title: The Ultimate Luxury
text: “Something along the lines of a hammer or throwing-weapon Seven Star Weapon might manage it. A frying pan leans toward blunt weaponry, and a kitchen knife just barely qualifies as a throwing weapon.”

Oh ho… so Big Sister can do it too? Come to think of it, Big Sister had also been rather taken aback by the sheer might of Father’s cooking skills. Perhaps if she copied Father’s frying pan, she could have gotten close to his level, I say. But—in my memory, Big Sister is making a sour face and shaking her head. How modest of her, indeed.
“In any case, Ren-san, this marks the end of Kelsus, the tournament-crashing menace of the dark culinary world.”
“C-come on! Once in a while can’t hurt, can it?”
“You haven’t learned a thing, have you. Did you actually come to enjoy the thrill of cooking that much?”
Ren fell silent at that. It seemed even he understood that what he’d come to love wasn’t cooking itself, but winning.
“At this rate you’ll end up just like a reincarnator, Ren-san. Is that really alright with you?”
“It’s not alright… but Itsuki, it’s not all bad, you know. Thanks to this, I managed to flush out and capture reincarnators who’d been hiding out in the culinary world.”
“Well, I suppose that tracks. Power-ups through food, brainwashing, forces that control whoever they feed and make them do as they please—sounds about right.”
“Yeah. Those guys had even bribed the judges, but once Naofumi’s knife got involved, the judges did a complete about-face. It was almost funny how easy the arrests turned out to be.”
Itsuki let out a deep sigh at Ren’s words.

“Honestly… a knife from Naofumi-san’s Sacred Weapon that grants cheats surpassing the reincarnators’ own superpowers… no, more accurately, I suppose it’s the sword’s Sacred Weapon at work. Ah, that explains it—I’d always wondered why you were unusually good at rounding up reincarnators back then, Ren-san. Now it makes sense.”

Indeed it does. Even accounting for advice from me and Rival, Ren had been catching them at a startlingly efficient rate. It moved just as fast as it had in the loop where Ren reunited with Fleon-chan, so I’d assumed Black Thunder’s influence was gradually accelerating his awakening.
“Either way, thanks to your rampage, Ren-san, the problem’s probably been wiped out. Worst case, we can just let Naofumi-san go on a rampage through the dark culinary world himself.”
Saying this, Itsuki turned to face me.
“Has Naofumi-san done anything like that in past loops?”

“Who can say, I say? He may well have. But it’s not as though I was glued to Father’s side the entire time. Besides, I feel no particular obligation to go out of my way to duel a bunch of reincarnators, I say.”
“Those guys turn violent the moment they lose. I can’t count how many times I got ambushed on my way home.”
“Ah, I see… so that’s the trick behind all those mysterious disappearances and social erasures…”

They’d been struck down by Ren in retaliation, captured as reincarnators, and dealt with accordingly. Incidentally, Rival made contact with the Zeltoble crowd, and apparently some of the captured reincarnators were sold off as entertainment on Seven Island to help fund Melromarc’s reconstruction.

“I understand now why the first Naofumi-san kept his distance from Motoyasu-san. In this loop, let’s have Naofumi-san put in the effort. Ren-san, if you cook while Naofumi-san is away, you’ll score points with the village children.”
“Why are you suddenly aiming for popularity points there!”

“So you don’t end up single forever. These days, men who can cook tend to be more attractive to women, don’t they? Even scoring points with Éclair-san or Wyndia-san works fine. Let’s rack up some brownie points.”
Ren seemed to accept Itsuki’s proposal, nodding several times before—
“But if I make it, won’t people just say it’s Naofumi’s cooking?”
“Well, it won’t taste exactly the same, but… it can’t be helped, since it isn’t your own original cooking to begin with.”
Of course not—the weapon is merely imitating Father’s cooking, after all.
“I think there’s value even in just being able to reproduce it. As long as they see you in the act of cooking, I doubt anyone will mind.”
“But still… becoming everyone’s errand boy like Naofumi…”

“Ren-san, you rely on Naofumi-san constantly, yet you look down on him a little, don’t you? It’s precisely because he pays that kind of attention to everyone that this place holds together. Neglect that, and you might not be a reincarnator, but you’ll still end up getting your comeuppance.”
“Hmm…”
Just then, Father returned to the village via portal.
“I’m home! Oh, everyone’s already back in the village.”
“O-oh. Welcome back, Naofumi.”
Ren greeted Father while carefully choosing his words, I say.
“I heard something about Ren crashing a tournament…”
“Er… apparently he was entering to defeat reincarnators hiding in the culinary world.”
“Huh. So Ren can cook too. Want to make dinner today?”
“N-no. Naofumi, please cook. I’ve made too much, I’m exhausted.”
“Really? Alright then, let’s see what to make…”
Father put on an apron and took his place in the kitchen, I say.
“Anyone have requests?”

Father was saying something suspiciously reminiscent of a devoted housewife, I say. However, in this world, Father is already wed to both Big Sister’s Older Sister and Panda. Which is to say—he’s a married man!

I recall, once, a certain hopeless-at-cooking pig attempting something along these lines and failing miserably. In the end, somehow, I ended up being the one to cook. Truly, as expected of Father—he accomplishes with the ease of breathing what those wretches could only fail at, I say!
“Let’s see… we already had Naofumi-san make spaghetti Napolitan and golden bunny-pil stew the other day… What menu would best capture the ultimate luxury of having Naofumi-san cook for us?”
“What’s gotten into you, Itsuki? Your words seem sharper than usual—more precisely aimed, somehow.”
“It’s all in the spirit of expanding Ren-san’s cooking repertoire—Naofumi-san’s dishes make excellent study material. Ren-san, Motoyasu-san, any suggestions?”
“Eh? Hmm…”
Ren crossed his arms and began pondering.
“Calculating… processing… processing…”
Rafumi kept churning away at the calculation of what to make. Break down already, I thought! But no—this was my chance to drill into Ren and Itsuki the ultimate luxury of a request made to Father.
“Then allow me to propose a menu to request from Father, I say.”
“You have something in mind?”
“What is it?”
“There’s a strange atmosphere all of a sudden… what do you want to eat?”
Fufufu… this is precisely what the ultimate luxury entails, I say!
“Father, I request that you recreate instant cup ramen, I say.”
“Wha…”
“No way…”
Ren and Itsuki were both left speechless. Fufufu… you two have no idea just how magnificent Father truly is, I say!
“Father, both Ren and Itsuki cannot forget the taste of their homeland. That is why they’ve been honing their skills and experimenting with all manner of trial and error, I say.”
“Ahh… I guess that makes sense. Alright, got it. I’ll go make it. Oh, and Motoyasu-kun, Ren, I’ll need fire and water magic later.”
“Leave it to me, I say.”
“A-ah…”
“Ah, for the flavor—soy sauce? Seafood? Curry? Or maybe a limited edition?”
“Soy sauce, I say.”
“OK.”
With that, Father headed off toward the back of the kitchen. Once he was out of earshot, Itsuki and Ren crept closer and whispered to me.
“What exactly is this outrage—gathering the finest ingredients and the finest chef, only to have him make the most lowbrow dish imaginable…”

“This, I say, is what constitutes the ultimate luxury. In the very first world, when Ren and I once let it slip without thinking, Father apparently wanted to try it himself and recreated it for us, I say.”

‘Sometimes you just crave junk food, you know? There are moments where I think about how I can’t go back to the modern world,’ Father had said as he made it. It seemed Father held no prejudice whatsoever against junk food. Something about how, once when he returned to the modern world, he’d gone to a family restaurant with Big Sister. I’d have thought something made from scratch would taste far superior, but I suppose junk food has its own particular charm. Come to think of it, I once heard that some billionaire in my world was devoted to cheap hamburgers from a certain discount chain. Which is to say—that must be the very same principle at work here!
“But… Naofumi-san, I’d heard that you can generally reproduce any dish you’ve eaten once, but can you really replicate even the noodles and that exact flavor?”
“I’ve heard instant noodles are fried in oil, but… how on earth do you even reproduce the flavoring?”
“You’ll understand once you try it, I say. When Father gets particularly invested, he even recreates the container itself, I say.”
“How far does this go…”

Caught between anticipation and dread, Ren and Itsuki waited for the requested dish to be completed. Partway through, I too was called in to help Father with the cooking. And then, at last—clunk—cups of not-yet-hot-watered instant cup ramen were set down before Ren, Itsuki, and myself. Of course, Father also brought along a kettle of hot water.

Ren and Itsuki gulped nervously before pouring the hot water from the kettle into their cups and waiting three minutes. Then, trembling, they picked up their chopsticks, grabbed some noodles, and brought them to their mouths.
It seemed both Ren and Itsuki had come to grasp the sheer magnitude of Father’s culinary prowess.
“How is it? I don’t know if it’s the exact same as the cup ramen from your worlds, but this is what it tastes like in mine.”
“I-it’s fine. More than fine—the flavor, the texture, everything about it is a perfect match… I’d honestly suspect this cup was summoned straight from Japan, it’s that identical.”
“Wouldn’t it be funny if a Hero Summoning brought forth cup ramen instead? Like some sort of Noodle Hero?”
Father joked cheerfully like that, but Ren and Itsuki had both gone pale in unison. Something seemed to be troubling them deeply—whatever could it be, I wonder?
“Is this the taste of Motoyasu-sama’s homeland?”
“Indeed it is, I say. In my world, it’s an extremely cheap, everyday dish for common folk. But in this world, it’s a magnificent feat of culinary reproduction that borders on the impossible, I say.”
“I see! How wonderful!”
Yuki-chan seemed to understand perfectly once I explained it to her, I say.
“Naofumi-san, even the mystery meat has been perfectly recreated, but what exactly is this meat?”
“Ah, even I don’t know that one…”
“You two don’t know either? You can generally tell just by eating it—this is—”

Heh. Before Father, deciphering the ingredients of mere instant food is a trivial matter, I say. Father proceeded to explain to Ren and Itsuki, in great detail, the manufacturing process behind cup ramen’s mystery meat. Apparently, incorporating magic partway through was the trick to easily reproducing it in this world.
“So, more or less like that. To get it exactly right takes nothing but practice, really. Recreating a lost flavor under all sorts of constraints is quite the challenge, you know.”
“Naofumi-san, did you do this sort of reproduction work back in Japan too?”

“Professors and lecturers would ask me sometimes, but there were times it put me in a bind when they’d request something I’d never actually tasted myself. One particularly tricky case—they asked me to recreate a discontinued candy from that ‘the-more-you-knead-it’ series. Honestly, that felt less like cooking and more like chemistry.”
“Haah… I suppose the sword’s Sacred Weapon’s judgment was correct after all. Wouldn’t you say, Ren-san?”
“Yeah…”
“What’s correct?”
Father tilted his head in confusion, but Ren and Itsuki offered no further explanation. In any case—truly, as expected of Father!
“Well, cup ramen aside, if Ren’s actually interested in cooking, it’d help me out if you pitched in sometimes.”
“A-ah… maybe, if I feel like it.”

And so, from time to time, on a whim, Ren began cooking Father’s dishes. Though, admittedly, the flavor never quite measured up to Father’s own cooking—that remained the one persistent flaw, if you could call it that. To begin with, Ren normally spent his days learning various things from the old man at the weapon shop, so it really was only an occasional thing. And thus, the extermination of the dark culinary world’s marauder and the eradication of cooking-related reincarnators steadily progressed.
“Dah-dah!”
“Kyah-kyah!”
“Itsuki, how long are you going to keep hogging that kid? Let me hold one too.”
“Not yet, Ren-san. Honestly, these kids are so full of energy it’s surprisingly hard to keep a grip on them.”
Today, everyone had gathered to see the babies born in Panda’s village, I say.
“M-make sure you’re holding them properly. They’re full of energy, but they were just born, after all.”
“Rah-fuu.”
“Eh, um…”
Big Sister, the Raph-species, and Mole all watched with worried expressions as Itsuki and Ren hoisted up the lively babies.
“Wow… I honestly wondered what kind of monster might be born while they were still in the womb, but now that they’re actually here, they’re surprisingly lively and adorable babies.”
“Total baby pandas, through and through!”

Both Itsuki and Ren, for once, seemed genuinely charmed as they cradled and doted on the babies. Might I suggest, though, directing some of that adoration toward Filolial-sama as well? The chick Filolial-samas are quite adorable too, I say!
“Dah!”
The baby’s hand crackled with sparks, and a bamboo shoot suddenly sprouted from the ground. Itsuki, flustered, cast a spell-interruption spell to disperse the bamboo shoot.
“…As lively as ever, it seems.”
“Kyah-kyah!”
Crackle, crackle—Big Sister’s Older Sister’s baby was likewise generating static electricity all around it.
“No question it’s adorable, but… it’s a little scary how it looks about ready to stand up and start running any second.”
“Ara~”

Incidentally, according to Father, Big Sister’s Older Sister’s baby had actually been born earlier. Apparently, Big Sister’s Older Sister had gone out for a light swim, as part of her daily routine, when she went into labor in the water—or perhaps she hadn’t even realized it, given how astonishingly effortless the birth was. She simply scooped the baby up and swam home, startling everyone upon her return. As for Panda, she did go through proper labor, though it didn’t take much time at all—both the midwife dispatched from Siltvelt and the village midwife were reportedly astounded, declaring they’d never seen such a sturdy, effortless birth. Come to think of it, the first world had been much the same. Something about how heroes’ children are remarkably hardy, and the mothers face no complications either, I say.
“Whoa… this kid was just born, but it’s already got quite a grip.”

The panda baby had latched onto Itsuki’s arm and was attempting to dangle from it. The whole scene looked exactly like a bear cub, though occasionally the baby would shift into a human infant’s form as well, I say.
